topic.title: Unpopular Opinion, Popular Take
topic.claim: Half the 'unpopular opinion' captions on Indian Instagram are extremely popular opinions wearing a disguise.
topic.behaviour: An account captions an obvious take as controversial purely to bait comments.
topic.mechanism: Disagreement gets more reach than agreement, so everyone manufactures a fight in the caption.
topic.group: anyone who writes or reads opinion captions
real_details: A comparison post ranking two old Bollywood comedies against each other drew pushback calling it a popular opinion, not unpopular
A commenter noted Hungama was actually the bigger hit in theatres and on TV, undercutting the 'unpopular' framing
Multiple commenters piled on to repeat and riff on the same iconic dog/hippopotamus exchange from the film
One commenter called Paresh Rawal's performance a comedy goldmine, a widely shared sentiment rather than a fringe take
Another added that the actress playing the wife was underrated, again a view many agreed with rather than argued against
topic.why_now: this caption trick is on nearly every opinion post right now

score.why: Calls out a caption trope people actually post, sharp and a little mean the way her rants are, without punching down at anyone real.

edits: slide 4: swap 'reads all that typing as a fire' for 'sees all that typing and thinks people care', so a 5th grader gets it on the first read.
slide 5: cut 'The account got its reach.' The next line already makes the point.
slide 3: change 'nobody argues' to 'nobody really argues', since slide 2 mentions some pushback.

paragraphs: Every 'unpopular opinion' post has the same comment section. Everyone agrees with it.
Take a typical one. Someone says Andaz Apna Apna is underrated. Caption: unpopular opinion.
The comments: "this is literally the popular opinion."
The label is for the comment box.
Agreement gets a like and a scroll. Disagreement gets a reply, then a reply to that reply, then a whole thread under it.
So now every take wears the costume. Chai over coffee, unpopular. Your mother's rajma is the best, unpopular. Sleep is nice, deeply unpopular.
Soon someone will call the monsoon wet and brace for the hate.
A truly unpopular opinion never needs the label.
You can tell from the comments. They're quiet, and a little angry.

draft.caption: Unpopular opinion: this post is also bait. Did it work?
draft.alt_text: A seven-slide text carousel about Indian Instagram posts captioned 'unpopular opinion' that are actually popular. It uses a typical example of a post ranking two old Bollywood comedies, where commenters mostly agree, quote famous lines and praise Paresh Rawal. It explains that disagreement drives reach, so captions fake a fight, and ends by saying a truly unpopular opinion never needs the label.

hook_candidates.hook: Enough with the 'unpopular opinion' posts. Every single comment agrees with you. And I know exactly why you keep typing it.
There's something odd about Indian Instagram. People post an 'unpopular opinion,' and then the whole comment section agrees.
The most popular thing on Indian Instagram right now is the unpopular opinion. And I know how that sounds.
Every 'unpopular opinion' on Indian Instagram right now: Chai beats coffee. Mom's rajma is the best. Sleep is nice.
I'm done. Saying chai beats coffee is not an unpopular opinion. Nobody is coming for you. So why does everyone keep pretending?
